description: Real Oregon road corridors whose geometry comes from U.S. Census Bureau TIGER/Line 2025 county road centerlines. This pilot carries geometry evidence only: a named road in a government centerline dataset is not evidence of legal public access, of a surface, or of a practical wildlife road cruise.

candidates.name: NW Cornelius Pass Rd

evidence.statement: Corridor geometry is the composition of the TIGER/Line 2025 features named NW Cornelius Pass Rd in Washington and Multnomah County.

provenance.method: Name-filtered bounded extract, duplicate links collapsed; see docs/ROADS.md

evidence.statement: A hill road that crosses the Willamette Valley / Coast Range boundary may merit habitat and wildlife-crossing checks.

questions: Where is the road legally open to public vehicles along its whole length?
Which stretch has the highest collision or roadkill potential?
What is the surface and shoulder condition today?

candidates.name: NW Springville Rd

evidence.statement: Corridor geometry is the composition of four TIGER/Line 2025 features; two source gaps remain unresolved and are reported instead of bridged.

provenance.method: Source-feature composition with a 150 m junction tolerance; see docs/ROADS.md

evidence.statement: The corridor changes ecoregion between the valley floor and the forested foothills, which may concentrate wildlife movement.

questions: Which feature or landowner occupies the 246 m gap between source segments?
Is any part of the road gated, posted, or privately maintained?
Where does the ecoregion transition actually fall on the ground?

candidates.name: NW Susbauer Rd

evidence.statement: Corridor geometry is a single TIGER/Line 2025 source feature with no duplicate links and no unresolved gaps.

questions: Is public vehicle access documented for this road today?
Do farm crossings or drainage ditches create wildlife-attractive edges?
